name: Essential Countdown Timer Bar
summary: Shopify countdown timer app for announcement bars, product pages, landing pages, carts and emails, with dated, recurring and evergreen timers, geo-targeting and a free plan; priced on how many times the timers load each month.
best_for: Shopify merchants who run real, dated promotions, launches or shipping cut-offs and want a top-bar, product-page or cart countdown without code, starting on a free plan
skip_if: your timers load tens of thousands of times a month and you are not ready to pay $29.99 for unlimited views, because on a lower plan the timers are switched off three days after you pass the limit; or your offers do not actually end, in which case a countdown is a claim you cannot stand behind
honest_knock:
The free plan is smaller than it looks, because of what counts as a view. The help centre says a view is every time a timer loads: a shopper who refreshes the page, or browses three product pages with a timer on each, adds several views, and two timers on one page count twice. A thousand views a month is a few hundred browsing sessions on a store with a top bar on every page. Starter's 10,000 and Essential's 50,000 are counted the same way.

Running out does not cost money; it switches the timers off. There is no overage charge. When you reach the limit you get an email, and if you have not upgraded within three days every published timer is unpublished until views reset on the 1st of the month. The month you are most likely to hit the ceiling is the month of your biggest sale, so on a Black Friday campaign that is when the countdown disappears. If a promotion depends on the timer, size the plan on the traffic you expect at the peak rather than last month's, or watch the usage in the app while the campaign runs.

The cart timer, the one that tells shoppers their items are reserved, starts on the $9.99 Essential plan, not on Starter. Whether a claim like that is true depends on how you set it up, and the FTC treats false urgency and scarcity as deceptive practice; an evergreen fixed-minute timer starts fresh for each visitor, so keep it for offers that work that way. One incident is worth knowing about: a Chilean merchant with nearly three years on the app wrote that Shopify Support had traced a checkout button that redirected customers to an outside URL to a security vulnerability related to this app. Essential Apps replied that it fixed the issue within two hours of the first report, resolved the cause the same day and reported the incident to Shopify. We found no report of a repeat.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month for up to 10,000 timer views, or $67.08 a year
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/essential-countdown-timer and in our own test the same day; read 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-21 there, on essential-apps.com/countdown-timer and in the vendor's help article on timer views) Four plans priced on monthly timer views. Free covers up to 1,000 views a month with unlimited product-page and top-bar timers. Starter is $6.99 a month, or $67.08 a year at a stated 20% saving, for up to 10,000 views, and adds landing-page timers and scheduled and recurring timers. Essential is $9.99 a month or $95.88 a year for up to 50,000 views, and adds cart timers, email timers, placing timers by product tag and geo-targeting. Professional is $29.99 a month or $287.88 a year for unlimited views and every premium feature. Paid plans carry a 7-day free trial, and the vendor's own site adds a 30-day money-back guarantee. A view is counted every time a timer loads, not once per visitor. There is no overage charge: past the limit you get an email, and if you do not upgrade within 3 days every published timer is unpublished until views reset on the 1st of the month. All charges are in USD, billed through Shopify every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps, with an address in Vilnius, Lithuania; the listing gives a launch date of 10 February 2022 and showed 1,721 reviews on 21 October 2026 and 1,736 at 5.0 on 17 November 2026. In our own test that day the app's plan page showed the same amounts, monthly and yearly, and Shopify's approval screen for Starter asked for a payment method.

compare_with.name: Scarcity.AI
compare_with.why: Scarcity.AI is the closest comparison in our own dossiers: its developer also publishes a countdown timer, next to a low stock counter and a live visitors counter. On our reading of 22 August 2026 that countdown listing showed a free tier and no paid ladder, while Essential Countdown Timer Bar starts free at 1,000 timer views a month and charges $6.99, $9.99 or $29.99 for more views and for cart, email, scheduled and recurring timers. The difference is scope. Scarcity.AI spreads urgency over three small apps, each installed and billed on its own, and its stock counter reads your real inventory; Essential puts every kind of countdown in one app and prices it on how often the timers load. A store that also wants stock and visitor signals fits Scarcity.AI; a store that mainly needs dated countdowns in several places, including carts and emails, fits Essential.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Essential Countdown Timer on a Shopify development store: the install (the first submit of the Install button did not install, the second did), the free plan without a card or plan screen, a top bar timer that reached an editor preview Hurry up! Sale ends in: 23 : 59 : 48 with a Shop now! button after 4 steps and about 2 minutes (not published, nothing saved, not seen on the store), the Pricing plans page with the free plan and three paid plans, the Shopify approval screen for Starter (a 7-day free trial; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Publishing, the view limit and the paid timer types were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the test started at 21:16 (Mac clock) on the App Store listing of Essential Countdown Timer by Essential Apps, which said Free plan available. Free trial available., a rating of 5.0 from 1,736 reviews. The Install button did not work for our test tool: the first submit of the install form landed on the list of apps without an install, and after the form target was set to the same tab the second submit showed the dialog Install app, which said that the app needs access to View staff and contributor data (Store owner) and View and edit store data (Products, Online Store, Shopify admin). Install was clicked and the app opened at once on the Free Plan, without a plan screen and without a payment screen. No account on the vendor site, password, card or phone number was asked. The Home of the app also showed a note about a partner programme (Partners earn 30% commission, First payout at $100) and a Q4 offer of 5 apps for $99 a month; neither was clicked. Core action, a top bar timer: Home, Create a new timer, Choose timer type (Product page, Top/bottom bar, Landing page marked Available with Starter plan, Cart page marked Available with Essential plan, Email timer and Checkout deadlines), Select this timer type on Top/bottom bar. After 4 steps and about 2 minutes from the start the editor stood there with the label Not published and a preview Hurry up! Sale ends in: with 23 : 59 : 48 (Hrs, Mins, Secs) and a button Shop now!. The Timer Type was Countdown to a date by default; Daily recurring timer was greyed out. The preview also showed a block Combine with Essential Loyalty with a button Install free, which was not clicked. The timer was NOT published, no theme change was made and nothing was saved; the preview was seen in the app only and not on the store, so how the bar looks on the store and how it behaves for a visitor are not known. No code was needed to get the preview. Plans in the app (Pricing plans): You're currently on Free Plan (0 / 1000 monthly views). One visitor can have multiple views per session. The Free Plan has Up to 1000 monthly views, Unlimited product timers and Unlimited top bar timers. Monthly view: Starter $6.99, Essential $9.99 and Professional $29.99, each with Start FREE 7-days trial. Yearly view (Save 20%): Starter $5.59 a month ($67.08 billed once a year), Essential $7.99 ($95.88) and Professional $23.99 ($287.88); which view was shown first on opening was not noted. Starter: up to 10 000 monthly timer views, Everything in Free, Unlimited landing page timers, Scheduled timer and Recurring timer. Essential: up to 50 000 monthly timer views, Everything in Starter, Unlimited cart page timers, Unlimited email timers, Adding timer using product tags, Geolocation targeting and Translations. Professional: unlimited timer views and all premium features. Under the plans the app showed 30 Day Money Back Guarantee - No questions asked!; the refund itself was not tried. Checkout: Start FREE 7-days trial on Starter (monthly) opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the plan starter, $6,99 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $6,99 plus any applicable taxes, Total $6,99 Due 24 Nov, a row Add payment method and the line By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. The Approve button was greyed out. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed, and a payment method was needed. No card was entered and nothing was approved; Cancel was clicked and the Free Plan stayed active. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was nothing to cancel in the app. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the row of the app and Uninstall: the dialog says that you can no longer use the app and that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and it asks for a Reason for uninstalling (Select all that apply) and optional feedback; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. Differences from the review: the listing showed 1,736 reviews where the review says 1,721 (read earlier; only the count differs); the 30-day money-back guarantee that the review attributes to the vendor site was also shown in the app, under the plans. The prices of the review (monthly Free 1,000 views, $6.99, $9.99, $29.99; yearly $5.59, $7.99 and $23.99 a month, $67.08, $95.88 and $287.88 a year) match the app. The locked timer types (landing page timers from Starter, cart page timers from Essential) match the review. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: publishing the timer to the store and seeing it in the theme or on the live store, the view limit of 1000 and what happens after it is passed (the review says timers are unpublished three days later), how views are counted, the paid timer types (landing page, cart page, email, scheduled, recurring), checkout deadlines, low-stock or visitor signals (not part of this app), the refund and the payment. Clean up: the Approve screen was left with Cancel, nothing was approved and the Free Plan stayed active. The app was uninstalled on 17 November through Settings, Apps with the required reason and no longer showed under installed apps. No timer was saved or published and no theme change was made. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Install button in the App Store did not install the app at the first try for our test tool. The Home of the app and the editor preview show promotions for other apps of the vendor (a Q4 offer of 5 apps for $99 a month, a block Combine with Essential Loyalty with Install free). The app says that one visitor can have multiple views per session, so the 1000 views of the free plan are not 1000 visitors.
